result.title: Multimodal Cross-Condition Learning for Temporal Sentence Grounding in Videos
result.summary: Temporal sentence grounding requires a video representation that preserves query-relevant evidence and a sentence representation that reflects the visual context in which it is interpreted. Prior end-to-end grounding addresses the first requirement through sentence-conditioned visual adaptation, but leaves the language representation independent of the video. This work proposes Multimodal Cross-Condition Learning (MCCL). Its Video Prefix Adapter (VPA) converts pooled visual context into a sequence of continuous tokens that condition a frozen DistilBERT encoder. Combined with the Sentence Conditioned Adapter (SCADA), VPA supports an ordered exchange from vision to language and back to vision. A comprehensive study examines two video backbones, LSTM and Mamba temporal modules, and four conditioning modes on two datasets. Bidirectional conditioning exceeds the stronger one-way mode by 1.6--2.3 mIoU points in all four Charades-STA settings. ActivityNet Captions exhibits a different pattern: bidirectionality helps I3D--Mamba, whereas video-to-text conditioning is stronger with C3D. The study extends one-way visual adaptation into a configurable multimodal framework and reports descriptive gains over the corresponding baselines.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出多模态交叉条件学习 MCCL：Video Prefix Adapter 把池化视觉上下文转成连续 token 去条件化冻结的 DistilBERT，与 Sentence Conditioned Adapter 构成「视觉→语言→视觉」的有序双向条件，并在两个数据集上比较 LSTM/Mamba 时序模块与四种条件模式。
AI.relevance_reason: 其以连续前缀 token 把视觉上下文注入冻结语言编码器内部状态的做法，可供核查 LVR 中视觉证据如何进入 latent 状态、是否被语言旁路化的问题；但论文本身是时刻定位任务，未涉及推理期 latent 生成或停止决策。
